title: Chemotherapy With Autologous B7-H3-CAR T Cells for Pediatric Patients With CNS Embryonal Tumors
official: Chemotherapy in Combination With Autologous B7-H3-CAR T Cells for Pediatric Patients With Recurrent, Refractory or Progressive CNS Embryonal Tumors
summary: This study is being done to learn about combining changed cells (CAR T-cells) with chemotherapy for children whose brain cancer has come back. Investigators want to find out if this combination helps fight the cancer and whether it causes any problems. In other words, they want to learn if it is helpful or harmful.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* ≤ 21 years of age at time of study enrollment
* Stratum A:

  * Histologically and molecularly confirmed diagnosis of medulloblastoma that is recurrent, refractory, or progressive. Central review verification of diagnosis must be completed by an institutional pathologist and can be from primary diagnosis or recurrence.
* Stratum B:

  * Histologically and molecularly confirmed diagnosis of a non-medulloblastoma, non-rhabdoid embryonal tumor according to WHO, that is recurrent, refractory or progressive. Central review verification of diagnosis must be completed by an institutional pathologist and can be from primary diagnosis or recurrence.
  * Eligible tumor types include, but are not limited to, Pineoblastoma, Embryonal tumor with Multilayered Rosettes (ETMR), embryonal tumor not elsewhere classified/not otherwise specified (NEC/NOS), CNS neuroblastoma, FOXR2-activated, CNS tumor with BCOR internal tandem duplication.
* Participants must have evaluable disease, defined as tumor that is measurable in two perpendicular diameters on MRI OR diffuse leptomeningeal disease OR clear MRI evidence of disease that may not be measurable in two perpendicular dimensions. A brain MRI with and without gadolinium and a spine MRI with gadolinium performed must be completed within 2 weeks prior to study enrollment to confirm disease.
* Tumors must be B7-H3 positive. B7-H3 expression will be evaluated by immunohistochemistry by an institutional pathologist (original tumor or recurrent specimen). A tumor is considered B7-H3 positive with an H-score ≥ 100.
* Able to tolerate apheresis. Participants who have previously undergone autologous apheresis at a FACT-accredited hematopoietic cell transplant and/or cell therapy program will be eligible for enrollment, if the existing apheresis product or T cells is sufficient for manufacturing the investigational product.
* Intraventricular access: administration of SJCARB7H3-41BBL-F2 will require the presence of an appropriate intraventricular access device (e.g. programmable ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt, or Ommaya reservoir). Participants are not required to have an existing intraventricular device at the time of study enrollment but must be willing and able to undergo a surgical procedure to have one placed prior to CAR-T cell therapy. See below for requirements regarding prior surgical procedures.
* Prior relapses: Disease history: Participant must have experienced at least one (1) and no more than two (2) relapses prior to study enrollment. Participants with primary refractory disease are eligible.
* Stratum A: Participant must have received prior CSI. Both Stratum A and B: Exception: Prior use of bevacizumab as monotherapy for the treatment or prevention of radiation necrosis is permitted
* Participants must have recovered from any surgical procedure before the commencement of bevacizumab therapy

  * At least 28 days has lapsed since a major surgical procedure
  * At least 14 days has lapsed since an intermediate surgical procedure
  * For participants who have undergone a minor surgical procedure, the wound must be closed, and at least 7 days must have elapsed prior to administration of the first planned dose of bevacizumab.
  * There should be no anticipation of need for major surgical procedures during the study Please note: Lumbar punctures or placement of PICC lines are not considered minor procedures and may occur at any time prior to or during therapy
* Chemotherapy: participants must have received their last dose of known myelosuppressive anticancer therapy at least 21 days (3 weeks) prior to study enrollment, or at least 42 days (6 weeks) if nitrosourea.
* Investigational/biologic agents: participants must have recovered from any acute toxicity potentially related to the agent and received their last dose of investigational or biologic agents ≥14 days prior to study enrollment. For agents that have known adverse events occurring beyond 14 days after administration, this period must be extended beyond the time during which adverse events are known to occur.
* Monoclonal antibody treatment and agents with known prolonged half-lives: participants must have recovered from any acute toxicity potentially related to the agent and received their last dose of the agent ≥ 21 days prior to study enrollment.
* Radiation: must not have received craniospinal irradiation within 24 weeks prior to enrollment. The tumor designated as "residual" for protocol purposes must not have received any radiation \< 12 weeks prior enrollment; focal radiation to areas of symptomatic metastatic disease must not be given \< 14 days of enrollment.
* For autologous stem cell rescue, ≥ 3 months must have elapsed prior to study enrollment.
* Neurologic status: participants with neurological deficits should have deficits that are stable for a minimum of 1 week prior to enrollment, without needing escalation of supportive care (e.g. corticosteroids). A baseline detailed neurological exam should clearly document the neurological status of the participant at the time of study enrollment.
* Seizures: participants with seizure disorders may be enrolled if seizures are controlled with no changes to dosage \< 7 days prior to enrollment, and they are on non-enzyme inducing anticonvulsants. Participants must not be taking enzyme-inducing antiepileptic medicines (including not limited to carbamezapine, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone) \< 7 days prior to study enrollment.
* Performance status: Karnofsky Performance Score (KPS for \> 16 years of age) or Lansky Performance Score (LPS for ≤ 16 years of age) must be ≥ 50% assessed \< 15 days prior to study enrollment.

  * Participants who are unable to walk because of neurologic deficits, but are up in a wheelchair, will be considered ambulatory for the purpose of assessing the performance score.
* Adequate bone marrow function \< 15 days prior to study enrollment defined as:

  * ANC ≥ 1000/µL;
  * Hgb ≥ 8.0 g/dL (may be supported);
  * Platelets ≥ 100,000/µL (unsupported)
* Adequate renal function \< 15 days prior to study enrollment: Serum creatinine ≤ 1.5x ULN as per age/gender below. Participants who do not meet the criteria in but have a 24-hour creatinine clearance or GFR (radioisotope or iothalamate) ≥ 70 mL/min/1.73 m are eligible.

  * Age 1 mo to \< 6 mo - Maximum Serum Creatinine (mg/dL): 0.4 (male), 0.4 (female)
  * 6 mo to \< 1 year - Maximum Serum Creatinine (mg/dL): 0.5 (male), 0.5 (female)
  * 1 to \< 2 years - Maximum Serum Creatinine (mg/dL): 0.6 (male), 0.6 (female)
  * 2 to \< 6 years - Maximum Serum Creatinine (mg/dL): 0.8 (male), 0.8 (female)
  * 6 to \< 10 years - Maximum Serum Creatinine (mg/dL): 1 (male), 1 (female)
  * 10 to \< 13 years - Maximum Serum Creatinine (mg/dL): 1.2 (male), 1.2 (female)
  * 13 to \< 16 years - Maximum Serum Creatinine (mg/dL): 1.5 (male), 1.4 (female)
  * ≥16 years - Maximum Serum Creatinine (mg/dL): 1.7 (male), 1.4 (female)
* Participants must have adequate renal function as demonstrated by urine protein screening, defined as follows:

  * Urine protein must be screened by dipstick analysis.
  * If urine protein is \< 2+ on dipstick, the participant is eligible.
  * If urine protein is ≥ 2+ on dipstick, a Urine Protein Creatinine (UPC) ratio must be calculated:

    * If UPC ratio ≤ 0.5, the participant is eligible.
    * If UPC ratio \> 0.5, a 24-hour urine protein collection must be obtained, and the result must be \< 1,000 mg/24 hours for the participant to be eligible.
* Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5x the upper limit of normal (ULN) for age
* SGPT (ALT) ≤ 3x ULN for age
* INR/PT ≤ 1.5x ULN
* Blood pressure ≤ 95th percentile on stable doses of medication without need of medication dose adjustments in the last 7 days.
* All systemically administered (i.e. subcutaneous, intramuscular, intravenous or per os) corticosteroid therapy (unless physiologic replacement dosing) must be stable or decreasing for ≥ 1 week prior to enrollment, with a maximum dexamethasone dose of 2.8mg/m2/day (0.5mg/kg/day methylprednisone) ongoing at enrollment. Corticosteroid physiologic replacement therapy for management of pituitary axis/adrenal axis insufficiency and/or topical administration (e.g. inhaled or dermatologic) is allowed.
* Participant and/or legally authorized representative has signed the Informed Consent Form for this study.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Pregnant women are excluded from this study.

  * Female participants of childbearing potential must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test within 15 days prior to enrollment. If the urine test is positive or cannot be confirmed as negative, a serum pregnancy test will be required.
* Female participants who are breastfeeding are not eligible for this study unless they agree to cease breastfeeding.
* Presence of a serious or non-healing wound, ulcer, or bone fracture.
* History of abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation, or intraabdominal abscess within 6 months prior to study enrollment.
* Known bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy.
* History of significant vascular disease (e.g. aortic aneurysm requiring a surgical repair, deep venous or arterial thrombosis) within the last 6 months prior to study enrollment.
* Evidence of new CNS hemorrhage on baseline MRI obtained \< 15 days prior to study enrollment.
* History of stroke, myocardial infarction, transient ischemic attack (TIA), severe or unstable angina, peripheral vascular disease, or grade II or greater congestive heart failure within the past 6 months prior to study enrollment.
* Serious and inadequately controlled cardiac arrhythmia.
* Participants taking NSAIDs, clopidogrel, dipyridamole, or aspirin therapy \>81mg/day \< 7 days of enrollment.
* Concurrent illness: any clinically significant unrelated systemic illness (serious infections or significant cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic or other organ dysfunction) that, in the opinion of the PI, would compromise the participant's ability to tolerate protocol therapy, put them at additional risk for toxicity, or would interfere with the study's procedures or results.
* Known immunodeficiency or known HIV infection.
* Prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history has the potential to interfere with the safety or efficacy assessment of the investigational regimen for this trial.
* Participant has a non-programmable ventriculoperitoneal shunt that could compromise ability to administer study therapy (in the opinion of the study PI).
* Rapidly progressive disease (in the opinion of the study PI).
* Participant and/or legally authorized representative unwilling to provide consent/assent for participation in the 15-year follow-up period, required if SJCARB7H3-41BBL is administered.
* Prior therapy Stratum A:

  * Prior therapy restrictions: Participant must not have previously received any of the following agents: bevacizumab, irinotecan and temozolomide
  * Exception: Prior use of bevacizumab as monotherapy for the treatment of radiation necrosis is permitted
* Prior therapy Stratum B:

  * Prior therapy restrictions: Participant must not have previously received any of the following agents: bevacizumab, irinotecan or temozolomide
  * Exception: Prior use of bevacizumab as monotherapy for the treatment of radiation necrosis is permitted
